title: Job Lifecycle, Resilience, and Operations
readerIntent: Configure, execute, restart, and recover jobs safely.
priorKnowledge: Know the job owner, schedule, handler, and side effects.
owner: CronJob definitions, scheduler, lifecycle services, and owning handler
summary: Create, update, run, start, stop, pause, resume, and remove operate on persisted definitions while runtime pools rebuild idempotently after restart.

sections.heading: Definition
items: Stable code, tenant, schedule, active state, handler, start/end, priority, node assignment, timeout, retry, overlap, idempotency, retention, and permissions.
Customer jobs belong in project modules; no arbitrary request service names, URLs, credentials, or executable handlers.

sections.heading: Resilience
items: Drain stops acquisition and process schedules while persisted definitions survive.
Node loss, network partition, and timeout can create uncertain outcomes; define duplicate policy, reconciliation, and compensation.
Retry only safe or explicitly idempotent work; process-local flags are not distributed locks.

sections.heading: Evidence
items: Positive, invalid, unauthorized, cross-tenant, schedule boundary, manual run, overlap, timeout, retry, restart, drain, node loss/return, recovery, reconciliation, performance, integration, and regression tests.
